segments.text: Good afternoon, this is Aakashwani and I am Saira Muchthaba with the mid-day news.
The headlines
India proposes developing joint India-ASEAN research agenda focused on maritime security
and emerging technologies. External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jai Shankar says,
world is moving towards new international order with wide range of countries playing
greater role in global affairs.
Wholesale price index inflation rises to 11.39% in September this year.
IMD forecast heavy rainfall over Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and
Karahekal for today.
And in cricket India to take on West Indies in 4th T20 International in Hyderabad today.
And now the news in detail.
Defense Minister Rajnath Singh has emphasized that India and ASEAN share a clear interest
in a peaceful, stable and open Indo-Pacific region.
Addressing the ASEAN-India Defence Think Tank Forum in New Delhi this morning, Mr Singh
said that ASEAN is central to India's Indo-Pacific vision, and that India's act-east policy
is a long-term commitment to working with Southeast Asia as an equal partner.
For India, ASEAN is central to our Indo-Pacific region.
India's ASEAN policies Sagar and Mahabharat region advocate open, multipolar cooperation
and we align these approaches through ASEAN-led mechanism. Our IACT policy is a long-term commitment
to working with Southeast Asia as an equal partner. Our collective objectives should be
to build trust, respect for each other's sovereignty and keep channels of dialogue open."
Mr Singh highlighted that the Indian Ocean and the waters of Southeast Asia constitute
a single connected maritime space, making its safety a shared responsibility. Pointing
According to the designation of 2026 as the ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation,
he called for strengthening maritime domain awareness, improving information sharing and
building collective capabilities to respond to emergencies, piracy and illegal fishing.
External Affairs Minister Dr. S. J. Shankar today said that consensus, mutual understanding
and self-interest would play a key role on the enforcement of rules agreed upon by
middle powers. Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi, Dr. Jay Shankar
emphasized that the era of a country dictating terms to others through threats is over. He
noted that the world is moving towards a new international order, with a wider range
of countries playing a greater role in global affairs. He added the current transition
should not be seen as a shift from order to disorder, but as the evolution of a
kind of order.
We now are heading towards a different kind of order.
The shareholding is changing.
The board of directors is expanding.
There is a much more active shareholders' discussion about where the company called Planet Earth
is going.
And there is a new understanding or a different understanding.
It may not be very neat, a bit messy, but at the end of the day a combination of what
you inherit, self-interest, some degree of what happens if it goes off the rails
that concern.
and that's how you evolve the order.
Dr. S.J. Shankar also said that India does not identify itself as a middle power, but
rather as a power in the middle.
The External Affairs Minister emphasized that India is the world's most populous country
with a GDP of around $4 trillion and has significant growth potential.
Union Electronics and Information Technology Minister Ashwini Vaishnav has said that
trust and cyber security are becoming increasingly important in the global semiconductor value
chain alongside cost considerations.
Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi today, Mr. Vaishnav said that
India aims to position itself as a trusted partner in semiconductor design, manufacturing
and testing of finished products.
The minister emphasized that developing a complete ecosystem is essential for sustainable
manufacturing.
The materials are very important because that ecosystem takes a lot of time and effort
to build.
So, we have to put in that extra effort to get that capability in our country in terms
of understanding of the materials, handling of the materials, manufacturing them, processing
them, storing them, using them in the chips or every other manufacturing process and making
sure that we develop an ecosystem which becomes good for us, good for the world.
Mr. Vaishnav has said that India is strengthening its economy. He said that India's public debt
to GDP ratio has declined from 61% to 55% over the past five years.
Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal has said that India has signed preferential trade agreements
with 38 developed nations over the past four years.
Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi today, Mr Goyal said India is
aiming to expand market access for Indian businesses while opening the country's markets
to global partners.
He noted that India's trade agreements covered economies with a combined GDP of around $10
trillion before 2014, which has now risen to approximately $70 trillion.
Our idea is to open India's market for the world as we wish to see other markets open
for us.
So from $10 trillion of GDP which was open to India on a preferential market basis
until 2014. Today, as we speak, we have trade agreements covering 70 trillion dollars of GDP.
Many other negotiations ongoing will take this figure up to about 85 trillion out of 115 trillion.
Canada and India have intensified negotiations for a comprehensive economic partnership agreement,
or SEPA, aiming to conclude the pact by the end of 2026, following the fifth round of talks in
Ottawa from October 5 to 9. The two countries are seeking to expand bilateral trade and investment
amid efforts to strengthen economic ties. Canadian International Trade Minister Manendra
Sidhu met commerce and industry minister Piyush Kohel in New Delhi this week on the sidelines
of a Canadian trade mission to Inter. According to Global Affairs Canada, the ministers
reviewed progress in negotiations and discussed ways to advance the proposed agreement.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined
by the mantra of Jan Seva Siddheesheva and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided
by this vision for Seva and Sushasana, the government has been ceaselessly working towards
achieving the goal of a vikasidh Bharat by 2047. Today in our special series we
bring you an instance of how this vision strengthened infrastructure in strategically
particularly important border areas, as a key pillar of India's development and national
security efforts, a report.
Located at an altitude of approximately 13,000 feet in Uruchal Pradesh, the Sehla tunnel
represents a significant engineering achievement in the challenging terrain of the eastern
Himalayas.
Built at a cost of around 825 crore rupees, the project comprises two tunnels measuring
approximately 1,003 m and 1,595 m in length.
It has been designed to provide more reliable connectivity between Tejpur in Assam and Tawang
in Urrachal Pradesh, particularly during periods of heavy snowfall and adverse weather conditions.
The tunnel holds immense strategic significance as it helps overcome the challenges posed
by the high altitude Sehla Pass.
Thus, improved connectivity facilitates the movement of armored forces, military equipment
and essential supplies thereby strengthening operational preparedness in this sensitive
border region.
Beyond its strategic importance, the project also carries significant benefits for local
communities.
More dependable road connectivity can improve access to healthcare, education, essential
services and markets while providing a boost to tourism and other economic activities.
The Sehla tunnel reflects India's continued emphasis on developing modern infrastructure
in remote and border areas, ensuring that geographical challenges do not become barriers
to progress.
A vital link between security and development, the Sehla tunnel stands as a symbol of engineering
excellence, improved connectivity, and the nation's commitment to strengthen its
border regions.
This is Ann Gulshan Rana for Akashwani News, from Jammu.
The Delhi government has passed a resolution congratulating Prime Minister Narendra Modi
on completing 25 years in public office.
Addressing a press conference in New Delhi, Chief Minister Righha Gupta said that Prime
Minister Modi has worked tirelessly and ceaselessly to improve the standard of living of the
country's citizens, foster progress and drive the development of states.
updates. This is Aakashwani giving you the news.
India's wholesale price index WPI based inflation rose sharply to 11.39% in September from 9.92%
in August on an annual basis. According to the provisional data released by the Ministry
of commerce and industry, the annual inflation last month was driven by higher prices of mineral
oils, food articles, crude petroleum and natural gas, coal and lignite, basic metals, chemicals
and chemical products, textiles, rubber and plastic products and electrical equipment.
Among the major categories in WPI, year-on-year inflation in the fuel and power group, surged
to 25.85% last month from 22.93% in August. Inflation in manufactured products rose to
9.76% from 8.37% and inflation in primary articles edged up to 8.67% from 7.76% during
the same period.
India has recorded a 21% decline in new tuberculosis cases between 2015 and 2024, compared to
were 12% global decline. According to WHO's Global Tuberculosis Report, the country's
TB treatment coverage has reached 92% against the global average of 78%. Our correspondent
reports that the government has intensified efforts towards eliminating tuberculosis through
expanded screening, advanced technology and community participation.
India's declining TB incidence reflects the impact of sustained public health efforts,
efforts, strong community participation, and continued commitment to strengthening
tuberculosis prevention and control initiatives across the country.
Under the TB Mukt Bhart Abhyan, more than 28 crore people have been screened.
Over 20 lakh individuals have received TB-preventive treatment, and 5,70,000 new NICSHM have joined
the initiative.
The National TB Elimination Program provides free screening and treatment services at
all public health facilities and private health care centers.
leaders. Health and Family Welfare Ministry has launched Josh Joint Squad for Health to
further strengthen community participation in India's fight against tuberculosis.
With Dipendra Kumar, Akshit Vadyana, Akashwani News, Delhi.
Delhi's Special Executive Magistrate Court, to date, remanded Kaukara Janta Party leaders
Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka to five days of judicial custody, while another leader
Ajinkya Rishinde has been released on a personal bond. The three were detained by Delhi
police over allegations of attempting to enter Jantar Mantar a day after it was denodified
as a protest site.
Facing criticism over the diesel deal with Russia, US President Donald Trump defended
the deal to release Russian diesel into global markets, saying it is intended to ease high
fuel prices and is not meant for the United States.
Trump said last Friday that Russia will supply more than 3 lakh tons of diesel followed
by 5 lakh tons in November and 1 million tons thereafter.
